reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Annotation
reg_knowledge.body:
35 rules. Sources: STD, MAN
ANN-001 Arial only: All annotation text is Arial; Satoshi and Clash Grotesk appear only inside the logo.
ANN-002 Printed heights: Notes and tags are 2.5 mm, view titles 3.5 mm, sheet titles 5 mm.
ANN-003 Kit text types only: Use only the FMC_Arial text types; never create a text type in a project.
ANN-004 Dimension text: Dimension text is Arial 2.5 mm.
ANN-005 Dimension units: Dimensions are in mm; levels in m to 3 dp, e.g. +3.150 FFL and 1193.150 m MSL.
ANN-006 Tags read parameters: A tag shows only parameter values, never typed text.
ANN-007 One tag per job: Use one tag family per job, e.g. FMC_TAG_E_Device for type and circuit.
ANN-008 Symbols by family: Every symbol is drawn by a family, never by lines on a legend.
ANN-009 MEP symbols keep readable: MEP device symbols print at 5 mm at both 1:50 and 1:100 through nested Keep readable symbols.
ANN-010 Symbol standards: Electrical symbols follow IEC 60617, safety signs ISO 7010, building symbols BS 8541-2, each verified before use.
ANN-011 Live legends: Legends are built from legend components or real annotation families; no drawn symbols and no empty rows.
ANN-012 MEP line colours by filter: MEP line types come from filters: cold water blue, hot red, soil brown, vent green dashed, storm cyan dash-dot, fire red, refrigerant purple, LP purple, earth green.
ANN-013 Black-line construction issue: Construction-issue views print black; tags carry the meaning, not colour.
ANN-014 General notes as legends: Statutory and general notes are LG_ legend views from 10_Notes, placed on Z-0002 or X-0001.
ANN-015 Sheet notes: A note for one sheet is an FMC_GA_SheetNote listed by the Z11_Sheet_Notes block filtered to that sheet.
ANN-016 Specification by keynote: An element's specification is shown by its keynote with FMC_TAG_Keynote, never typed.
ANN-017 Keynote label by view: Keynote tags show Key Value on plans and Keynote Text on details.
ANN-018 Keynote legend by sheet: Keynote legends are filtered by sheet so each sheet lists only its own keynotes.
ANN-019 Keynote picked from list: Keynotes are picked from the list, never typed.
ANN-020 Design data: Discipline design data comes from Project Information through a data panel or is typed once where marked [ ].
ANN-021 No fake model in 2D: Detail lines, filled regions and masking regions are for details only, never to fake a model element.
ANN-022 Fill patterns: Use only kit fill patterns; never create one in a project.
ANN-023 UK English: All drawing text is in UK English.
ANN-024 Abbreviations from register: Use only abbreviations from the kit register; common ones on Z-0003, discipline ones on X-0001.
ANN-025 Permit vs construction views: Permit and construction plans use separate view templates so permit sets hide construction clutter.
ANN-026 Stage 2 density: At RIBA stage 2 annotate room names and areas, grids and levels only.
ANN-027 Stage 3 density: At RIBA stage 3 add overall and grid dimensions, door and window tags, and level heads.
ANN-028 Stage 4 density: At RIBA stage 4 tag every room, door, window and wall type, dimension openings, and keynote construction plans.
ANN-029 Stage 5 density: At RIBA stage 5 add setting-out dimensions to grids, MEP tags and keynotes on all construction views.
ANN-030 Tidy: no overlaps: Tags, text and dimensions must not overlap each other or cross model linework where avoidable.
ANN-031 Tidy: leaders: Use a leader only when the tag is away from its element; leaders are straight, no crossing.
ANN-032 Dimension to references: Dimension strings reference grids, walls or reference planes, never loose points.
ANN-033 No overridden dimension values: Never override a dimension's value text.
ANN-034 Annotation never moves model: Annotation tools may move annotation only, never model elements.
ANN-035 Revision clouds: Revision clouds are tied to a Revit revision; free-drawn clouds are not used.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Claude Use
reg_knowledge.body:
27 rules. Sources: STD, MAN, RDM, CLM
AI-001 Live-model lock: Model-changing tools run only on families, new unsaved documents and library files; on a live project, say so and stop.
AI-002 No workarounds: Never retry a refused action through send_code_to_revit or any other route.
AI-003 Shared-models toggle: Setup tools run on shared or live models only while the user's toggle is on; Claude never asks to change it.
AI-004 Model tools stay locked: Model-class tools stay locked on live models even when the toggle is on.
AI-005 Never save workshared models: Tools never save or synchronise a workshared model; the user does that in Revit.
AI-006 Write roots only: Write files only to write roots (WIP and staging), never to 02_Shared, 03_Published, 04_Archive, 05_Incoming or 04_Families\<Role>.
AI-007 Nothing deleted: Nothing is deleted; archive moves a closed file to _Archive.
AI-008 Dry run and a clear yes: Every write starts as a dry run; show the result and get a clear yes before the real run.
AI-009 Names enforced: Use only standard names for models, families and templates; the server rejects anything else.
AI-010 Never decide for a professional: Claude never releases families, approves gates, changes structural sections, sets demand factors or signs anything.
AI-011 Automate repeatable, gate consequential: A named professional approves anything that changes design, cost or safety.
AI-012 Script output proves nothing: A parameter value, script output or stamp toggle never proves compliance or approval.
AI-013 Safety rules: Dry run first, one transaction, logged, fail loudly, never overwrite approved work.
AI-014 Kit is the only source: A value missing from the kit is a kit change request, never filled in by Claude.
AI-015 Never invent parameters: Never invent a shared parameter; report a missing one as a dictionary change request.
AI-016 Report every warning: Report every build warning as a hand step for the Family Librarian; never hide them.
AI-017 Read live models only: On live project models Claude reads and reports; it does not model them.
AI-018 Human-only list: People keep: family release, CDE gates, publishing templates, demand factors, structural sections, coordinates, worksharing and every signature.
AI-019 Structural sections: A suggested section change is only a proposal until the Structural Engineer of Record approves it in writing.
AI-020 Approved wording: Claude writes 'digital handover' and 'aligned with ISO 19650', never 'digital twin' or 'certified' without evidence.
AI-021 No unverified standards: Claude never puts a standard number in a deliverable unless it is Verified in the Standards Register.
AI-022 Photo dimensions: Dimensions Claude reads from a photo are estimates until a datasheet or the user confirms them.
AI-023 Counts not dumps: Claude asks for summaries and counts, not element dumps, and prefers one batch call over many.
AI-024 Log every run: Each tool run adds a row to FMC_MCP_FileLog.csv.
AI-025 Cite the rule when refusing: When Claude refuses or stops, it names the rulebook rule id and clause.
AI-026 Annotation edits on own views: Claude may tidy or add annotation only in views the user names, after a dry-run preview.
AI-027 Stage confirmed by user: Claude asks the user for the RIBA stage and issue set before building or checking a sheet set.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Families
reg_knowledge.body:
44 rules. Sources: STD, MAN, RDM, CLM
FAM-001 System family first: Use a system family wherever Revit has one; loadable families are for physical products.
FAM-002 One product, one family: One product is one family carrying all its data and all its connectors.
FAM-003 Right category, fixed: Build from the category's metric template and never change the category later.
FAM-004 Generic Model only as last resort: Use Generic Model only when no category fits, and then always with a code and an IfcExportAs value.
FAM-005 No import categories: A family has correct category and subcategories and no import categories.
FAM-006 Subcategories: Use subcategories for parts that view filters must control.
FAM-007 Origin at set-out point: Put the origin where the product is set out: door centre in the wall, device mounting point, equipment floor centre.
FAM-008 Reference planes: Name the planes Center (Left/Right), Front and Back, and mark them Strong.
FAM-009 Parameters drive geometry: Dimensions drive geometry, FMC shared parameters carry data, shared values are type parameters, and derived values use formulas.
FAM-010 Detail levels: Coarse shows a symbol or box, Medium the outline, Fine the full geometry; plans never show 3D clutter.
FAM-011 Type count: Keep up to about ten types in a family; beyond that use a type catalogue .txt beside the .rfa.
FAM-012 Face-based devices: All E, FP and M terminal devices are face-based; doors and windows stay wall-hosted.
FAM-013 Shared nesting sparingly: Tick Shared on a nested child only when it must be counted, tagged or circuited on its own.
FAM-014 Nested plan symbols: MEP plan symbols are nested FMC_SYM_* generic annotations with Keep readable on.
FAM-015 Adaptive components gated: Adaptive components need Head of Modelling approval and never replace a normal family.
FAM-016 Materials: Materials are parameter-driven and FMC_ named.
FAM-017 One keynote per type: Every type is one specification and carries one keynote: Revit Keynote equals FMC_Keynote_Code, a code that exists in FMC_Keynotes.txt. A type without a code stops the build and files a keynote request.
FAM-018 Connector classification: MEP connectors have the correct system classification and flow direction.
FAM-019 Electrical load connector: Load connectors link Voltage, Poles, Apparent Load, Power Factor, Power Factor State and Load Classification; motors use Lagging.
FAM-020 Voltage exactly 240 V: A single-phase connector voltage is driven by a type parameter holding exactly 240 V, not 230 V.
FAM-021 Part Type: Supply equipment sets Part Type to Panelboard, Switchboard, Other Panel or Transformer, never Equipment Switch.
FAM-022 No tray connectors on equipment: Equipment never carries a cable tray or conduit connector.
FAM-023 Pipe connectors: Pipe connectors link Diameter, Flow Direction, Flow Configuration and Fixture Units, with FMC_Discharge_Units beside them.
FAM-024 Duct connectors: Duct connectors link Size, Flow in L/s, Flow Direction and Loss Method.
FAM-025 ELV connectors: ELV devices carry one no-load connector per system they belong to.
FAM-026 IFC mapping: Set IfcExportAs / IfcExportType where the category default is wrong.
FAM-027 Size and cleanliness: Keep families under about 1 MB with no nested DWG and nested families purged.
FAM-028 Load test: Load test every family: place, flex all types, schedule, tag, export NWC and IFC.
FAM-029 Chain test: Connected families pass the chain test in FMC_ChainTest_<Role>.rvt with no warnings.
FAM-030 Stage support: A family provides what each G-stage needs: coarse scheme type (G2), true sizes and connectors (G3), approved product detail (G4), asset parameters (G5).
FAM-031 Release is human: Only the Family Librarian or BIM Manager releases a family to 04_Families\<Role>; tools build to _Staging.
FAM-032 Plan, dry run, build: Always plan first, then build as a dry run, then build for real after a clear yes.
FAM-033 Batches of 25: Build at most 25 families per batch and report every warning.
FAM-034 Dictionary parameters only: A recipe parameter missing from the dictionary is skipped and reported, never added another way.
FAM-035 Recipe server check: A recipe passes the schema, uses dictionary parameters only, follows FMC_ or D4 naming, and formulas name existing parameters.
FAM-036 Photo sizes are estimates: Sizes read from a photo are estimates; a datasheet or the user confirms them before a build.
FAM-037 Inject: Inject adds dictionary parameters, sets values, renames to the standard and saves to staging or the project WIP.
FAM-038 Batch families are project families: Batch output is named under D4 and saved in the project WIP.
FAM-039 Recipes build to LOD 400: Recipes build to LOD 400 Fine geometry (frames, profiles, rebates, fixings, interfaces); freeform shapes stay hand work.
FAM-040 In-place limit: More than five in-place families turns model health amber, fifteen red.
FAM-041 Groups and MEP: Never group circuited or connected MEP elements; groups have one nesting level at most.
FAM-042 Title block logos vector: Logos in title blocks come from 11_Brand as vector lines and filled regions, never raster images.
FAM-043 Recipe default dimensions: A recipe without a confirmed size uses the family register Types column; if absent, the build stops and asks.
FAM-044 Family line graphics: Family lines are black or dark grey; colour belongs to materials. Outlines and the Coarse envelope pen 3 (0.18 mm), detail edges pen 2 (0.13 mm), cut pen 4 (0.25 mm); pen 1 (0.10 mm) only for door swings, clearance zones, hidden parts and indications, in a colour no lighter than 45%. A deliberate exception is marked keep_graphics.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Links And Coordinates
reg_knowledge.body:
27 rules. Sources: STD, MAN, RDM
LNK-001 One shared system: Every model on a project shares one coordinate system fixed from the surveyor's control points.
LNK-002 Never move origin or zero base points: Nobody moves the Internal Origin or sets base points to 0,0,0 to make things line up.
LNK-003 Default CRS: Default CRS north of the equator is Arc 1960 / UTM zone 36N (EPSG:21096); otherwise the surveyor states it.
LNK-004 No datum mixing: Drone/GNSS data in WGS 84 (EPSG:32636) is transformed by the surveyor before use.
LNK-005 Near the internal origin: Model geometry stays within about 10 km of the Internal Origin.
LNK-006 Project Base Point: The Project Base Point sits at grid A/1 at FFL.
LNK-007 Survey Point: The Survey Point sits on a surveyor's control point with its easting, northing and MSL elevation, and is pinned.
LNK-008 Coordinate record: The coordinate record holds CRS and EPSG, control point, E/N/elevation, true north angle, PBP location and who verified it.
LNK-009 Spot check 5 mm: Two other control points tagged with spot coordinates must agree with the survey within 5 mm.
LNK-010 Pin base points: Pin the Survey Point and the Project Base Point.
LNK-011 Master grids and levels: Master levels and grids live in the site model; levels are above the project base (FFL).
LNK-012 Grids and levels by Copy/Monitor: Discipline models take grids and levels from the site model by Copy/Monitor; nobody draws their own.
LNK-013 First link Origin to Internal Origin: Each discipline first links the site model Origin to Internal Origin, then acquires coordinates.
LNK-014 Links by shared coordinates: After set-up every link uses Auto – By Shared Coordinates.
LNK-015 Refuse without shared coordinates: The link tool refuses when the files share no coordinates.
LNK-016 Deviation zero: After set-up the health check shows 0 mm Survey Point deviation.
LNK-017 Coordinates stay with people: Acquiring and publishing coordinates stays with the BIM Coordinator; tools never do it.
LNK-018 No re-acquire from consultants: Never re-acquire coordinates from a consultant's model without PIM approval.
LNK-019 Exports carry shared coordinates: NWC, IFC (with EPSG) and DWG exports use shared coordinates.
LNK-020 Link worksets: Each link sits on its own Z_Links_<Role> workset.
LNK-021 Halftone links: Linked models show halftone except the model being coordinated.
LNK-022 No systems across links: Circuits and pipe/duct systems cannot connect into a linked model; use FMC_Asset_Tag power connections instead.
LNK-023 Clean links before publish: Before publishing, links are unloaded or set to shared positions.
LNK-024 Link CAD: CAD is linked, not imported.
LNK-025 Read-only links from CDE: Published models, IFC and DWG may be linked from Z: as read-only.
LNK-026 Pin is Setup, audit is Read: Pinning links is a Setup action; link audit is Read and runs on any model.
LNK-027 Pin links: Pin every Revit link instance after placement.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Naming
reg_knowledge.body:
39 rules. Sources: STD, MAN, RDM
NAM-001 Container name pattern: Every file name has seven fields joined by hyphens: Project-Originator-Volume-Level-Type-Role-Number.
NAM-002 Project code: Use the client's project code; if there is none use F + two-digit year + three-digit number, with no hyphen.
NAM-003 Originator code: The originator is FMC for Formcraft; other parties use the 3–6 character code registered in the BEP.
NAM-004 Volume field: The volume field is ZZ, XX, 01–99, SW or a code the BEP defines.
NAM-005 Level field: The level field is ZZ, XX, 00, 01–99, B1–B9, M1 or RF.
NAM-006 Type code: The type field must be one of the Formcraft type codes.
NAM-007 Role code: The role field must be a Formcraft role code; F and X are reserved and never used.
NAM-008 Number field: The number is four digits, 0001–9999, unique within the other six fields.
NAM-009 Allowed characters: Inside a field use only capital letters and digits; no spaces, underscores or dots before the extension.
NAM-010 Path length: The full file path must be shorter than 200 characters.
NAM-011 Name never changes: Never put status or revision in a file name; they live in CDE metadata and the name stays for life.
NAM-012 Status codes: Status is one of S0–S4, S6, S7, A1…, B1… or CR, held as metadata.
NAM-013 Revision codes: Preliminary revisions are P01, P02…; WIP versions P01.01…; contractual C01, C02….
NAM-014 Library family file name: A library family file is FMC_[Role]_[CategoryToken]_[Description].rfa using an approved token.
NAM-015 Project family file name: A project family is [Project]_[Role]_[CategoryToken]_[Description].rfa and is saved only in 01_WIP\<Role>\Families\.
NAM-016 Family type name: A family type is named [KeySize]_[Variant].
NAM-017 System type name: Wall, floor, roof and ceiling types are named [Location]_[Core][Thk]_[Finish] with an approved location prefix.
NAM-018 No element code in type names: Never put the X.YYY_ZZ code in a type name; it lives in FMC_Keynote_Code.
NAM-019 Material name: Materials are named FMC_[Group]_[Description].
NAM-020 View template name: View templates are named VT_[Role]_[ViewType]_[Purpose].
NAM-021 View name: Views are named [Role]_[ViewType]_[Level/Zone]_[Purpose].
NAM-022 Working view prefix: Working views not on sheets start with WIP_.
NAM-023 Level name: Levels are named [LevelCode]_[Description] using the container level codes (00, 01, B1, M1, RF).
NAM-024 Workset name: Worksets are named [Role]_[Content].
NAM-025 Shared parameter name: Shared parameters are named FMC_[Name] with no spaces.
NAM-026 Schedule name: Company QA schedules are [NN]_[Subject]_[Purpose] (00–09); discipline schedules are [Role][NN]_[Subject]_[Purpose] from 10.
NAM-027 Annotation family name: Annotation families are FMC_TAG_[Role]_…, FMC_SYM_[Role]_…, FMC_GA_…, FMC_TB_… or FMC_DI_[Role]_….
NAM-028 Profile family name: Profile families are named FMC_Profile_[Use]_[Size].
NAM-029 Legend view name: Legend views are LG_[Role]_[Key], one per heading of the 10_Notes text.
NAM-030 Calculation IDs: Calculations are CA-[Role]-NN, with working sheets Calc_[Role]_[Subject].
NAM-031 Filter name: View filters are F_[Role]_[Subject] and are rule-based only.
NAM-032 Script name: Scripts are named FMC_[Verb][Object].dyn or .py.
NAM-033 Template file name: Templates are named FMC_<Role>_Template_v2.2.rte, plus FMC_Base_Template_v2.2.rte.
NAM-034 Sheet number: Sheet numbers are [Role]-[4 digits] using a sheet role.
NAM-035 Sheet name: Sheet names are plain words, e.g. "Ground Floor Plan — Block A".
NAM-036 Abbreviations registered: Any abbreviation not in the manual is added to the BEP abbreviation list before use; nobody invents codes in file names.
NAM-037 No default type names: Placed types must not keep Revit default or generic names.
NAM-038 Register IDs: Issues, decisions and change requests are numbered [Project]-ISS-0001, -DEC-0001 and -CR-0001.
NAM-039 Model group name: Model groups are named [Role]_GRP_[Description].

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Project Start
reg_knowledge.body:
24 rules. Sources: STD, MAN, RDM
PST-001 User picks the folder: The user creates the project folder and picks it; the tool builds the tree inside it.
PST-002 Standard folder tree: Build the standard project tree: 00_Info to 07_Cost with their subfolders.
PST-003 Empty folders only: The tree holds only empty folders and _README.txt files; nothing else goes into gate folders.
PST-004 Project code: The project code is 2–6 capitals and digits with no hyphen.
PST-005 Short name: The short name in the folder uses letters and digits only.
PST-006 Model from role template: Every model starts from its role template, never from Base.
PST-007 Model names: Discipline models are named [Project]-[Originator]-[Volume]-[Level]-M3-[Role]-0001.rvt in 01_WIP\<Role>.
PST-008 One model per role per volume: Make one model per role per volume; link other disciplines, never copy them in.
PST-009 Combined MEP is a deviation: A combined E/M/P/FP model is allowed only as a deviation recorded in the BEP.
PST-010 Site model first: Create the site model F26001-FMC-SW-XX-M3-Z-0001.rvt first; it holds only survey points, boundary, grids, levels and topography.
PST-011 Project Information once: Enter project details once in Project Information; title blocks and panels read them.
PST-012 Project Number equals code: Project Number holds the same value as FMC_Project_Code.
PST-013 Blanks visible: Unknown Project Information values stay TBC, never empty.
PST-014 CRS recorded: Write the CRS name and EPSG code into FMC_CRS in every model.
PST-015 Coordinate record before models: The PIM files the coordinate record before any discipline model is set up.
PST-016 Worksets at start: Create the template worksets at project start.
PST-017 Step by step with dry runs: Run folder, models, project info, links, families and QA in order, each with a dry run; the user may stop after any step.
PST-018 Write roots: After building the tree, add only <project_root>\01_WIP to the write roots.
PST-019 Ends at the people gate: Project start stops before worksharing, central location and coordinates; the coordinator does those.
PST-020 No live central in synced folder: Never put a live central model in a cloud-synced folder.
PST-021 Container name fixed for life: Once created, a model's container name never changes.
PST-022 Project families in WIP: The project family set is built under D4 names into 01_WIP\<Role>\Families\.
PST-023 Model size: Split a model when it exceeds about 400 MB or a sync takes longer than about 2 minutes.
PST-024 Default roles: Offer A, S, M, E, P, FP, LP, C and L as default roles, plus Z always and W for Formcraft-built work.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: QA
reg_knowledge.body:
31 rules. Sources: STD, MAN, RDM
QA-001 Separate RAG metrics: Report model health as separate red/amber/green metrics, never one score.
QA-002 Warnings: Total warnings turn amber at 100 and red at 300; list the top five by text.
QA-003 Uncoded types: Placed 5D types without a code turn amber at 1 and red at 20.
QA-004 Unknown codes: Any type with a code not in master data is red.
QA-005 Rooms: Unplaced or unbounded rooms turn amber at 1 and red at 5.
QA-006 CAD imports: Any imported (not linked) CAD is red.
QA-007 In-place families: In-place families turn amber at 5 and red at 15.
QA-008 Views not on sheets: Views not on sheets turn amber at 150 and red at 400.
QA-009 Survey Point drift: Survey Point deviation from the coordinate record turns amber at 1 mm and red at 10 mm.
QA-010 Default type names: Placed types on Revit default or generic names turn amber at 1 and red at 10.
QA-011 Missing geometry stage: Placed elements with no G-stage turn amber at 1 and red at 50.
QA-012 Off-millimetre lengths: Walls and beams with fractional-mm lengths at G3+ turn amber at 1 and red at 20.
QA-013 Reported-only facts: Report base point values, pinned state, links loaded, workshared, central location, cloud model and file size.
QA-014 Thresholds per project: Default thresholds may be changed per project in the BEP.
QA-015 Run cadence: Run model health weekly per model and before every issue.
QA-016 Four-step audit: Before Shared → Published, file evidence for model review, coordination, health (no RED) and data (QA schedules empty, 0 invalid codes, IDS pass).
QA-017 WIP → Shared checklist: Before sharing: synced, relinquished, sync run today, health no RED, name check, purpose and status set, links clean, model review for G3/G4.
QA-018 Name check: Check outgoing container names with the name-check rules.
QA-019 Bindings check: Report parameters missing, deprecated-but-bound, wrong binding or extra categories against the dictionary.
QA-020 Sheet QA: Check title block, number, role, status, issue set, view templates and container name on every sheet.
QA-021 QA views clear: QA views and schedules must be empty before issue; uncoded types are fixed by picking a keynote, unpriced ones go to the QS.
QA-022 IDS check: IFC deliveries pass the project IDS; a failed specification blocks the exchange unless the PIM records an exception.
QA-023 Purge before milestones: Purge unused before every milestone issue.
QA-024 Link CAD, never import: CAD is linked, never imported, in project models.
QA-025 Model review is human: The model review is held by the Head of Modelling or a Level 3 modeller; tools only prepare views and lists.
QA-026 Reports, not dumps: QA writes CSV and Markdown reports; Claude receives counts and the report path only.
QA-027 Read class: QA is read-only and may run on every model, including live ones.
QA-028 Naming scope until D3: QA reports file, sheet and type names; view and level names are reported as warnings only until D3 is decided.
QA-029 Release checks: Families, electrical chain, sheets, legends, notes, models and templates pass the STD release checks before production.
QA-030 Electrical chain: Every board shows a distribution system, and Calc_E_MaxDemand agrees with Revit within 2%.
QA-031 Annotation QA: Report sheet views missing a view template, typed text in tags, untagged doors and windows on construction plans, and overlapping tags.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Rhino
reg_knowledge.body:
17 rules. Sources: 
RHN-001 Millimetres and one tolerance: Rhino part files are in millimetres with an absolute tolerance of 0.01 mm and an angle tolerance of 1 degree.
RHN-002 Closed, manifold, valid: Every part is one closed, manifold, valid solid (a Revit form is made only from a closed solid).
RHN-003 No short edges: No edge is shorter than min_edge_mm (Revit drops curves under 0.78 mm); use a larger fillet or none.
RHN-004 Smooth, not faceted: Curved parts are NURBS surfaces (revolve, loft, sweep, pipe, fillet), never polygon outlines or meshes standing in for curves.
RHN-005 LOD 400 detail: At LOD 400 a part shows what is made: true section profiles and radii, real thickness, joints (tenons, welds, dowels where visible), fixings and hardware, and the parts the maker cuts as separate solids.
RHN-006 Rhino for fixed shapes, Revit for what flexes: Anything a type or instance parameter changes is native Revit geometry on reference planes; Rhino parts are fixed true shapes, placed by parameters and varied by type.
RHN-007 Named parts carry their data: Each part's layer is its name; it carries a subcategory, a kit FMC_ material and a visibility (fine, medium_fine or all).
RHN-008 Inside the envelope: No part is larger than the type's envelope, and no part sits more than envelope_error_mm outside the Coarse envelope.
RHN-009 Weight budget: A LOD 400 family stays under family_mb_max; more than mesh_faces_warn render-mesh faces is a warning to simplify.
RHN-010 Rhino proof before Revit: A recipe with Rhino parts builds in Revit only when every part passed the Rhino check and was exported under this rulebook, unchanged since (same SHA-256).
RHN-011 Complex shapes are proven in Rhino: A recipe marked rhino_required (a complex shape) has its curved parts as import_part from Rhino, not native stand-ins.
RHN-020 Reference evidence: A family made from a picture has a reference file: at least min_views views, min_sources sources (catalogue, datasheet, listing, standard or maker), min_verified_dimensions verified dimensions, evidence for each material, and a list of at least min_features signature features.
RHN-021 Generated views are not evidence: A view generated or traced by AI is marked kind generated; it may guide modelling but never counts toward min_views or as proof of size or material.
RHN-022 Looks like the reference: Before release, every reference view matches the same model view (IoU at least min_iou, width/height ratio within max_aspect_diff) and a blind reviewer marks every signature feature present.
RHN-023 Rhino likeness first: The likeness check runs on the Rhino renders before the Revit build, and again on the Revit family before release.
RHN-024 A person after the rounds: After max_rounds failed likeness rounds the family stops and goes to a person with the renders, the scores and what is missing.
RHN-025 No brands: Generic library families carry no brand or model; a client-line family may carry the client's own.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Shared Parameters
reg_knowledge.body:
21 rules. Sources: STD, MAN, RDM
SPR-001 Dictionary size: The dictionary has 178 parameters in 30 groups: 171 active and 7 deprecated.
SPR-002 Deprecated not bound: Never bind the 7 deprecated parameters; use the Revit built-ins instead.
SPR-003 File header: The shared parameter file header is META 2 1, as Revit writes it.
SPR-004 Stable GUIDs: GUIDs are generated (UUID v5 from the name) and never hand-edited.
SPR-005 Type or instance: Bind as Type when every instance shares the value, Instance when it belongs to the placed object, exactly as the dictionary says.
SPR-006 Listed categories only: Bind each parameter only to the categories listed for it.
SPR-007 No type/instance conflict: Never bind a parameter as Type in one template and Instance in another.
SPR-008 Data group: Bind FMC parameters under the Data group.
SPR-009 Bind dry run first: Run the bind as a dry run first, then bind everything in one transaction.
SPR-010 Conflicts reported: If a bound parameter conflicts with the dictionary, report it and change nothing.
SPR-011 Never change identity: Never change a GUID, rename a parameter or change its datatype.
SPR-012 Retire, don't reuse: Retire a parameter as Deprecated with Replaced_By; its line stays and its GUID is never reused.
SPR-013 New parameters by change request: A missing parameter is a dictionary change request approved by the BIM Manager; never create one by hand.
SPR-014 Read-only file: The shared-parameter file on the CDE is read-only for everyone except the BIM Manager.
SPR-015 Source of record: The Parameters sheet of FMC_Master_Data.xlsx is the source of record for datatype, binding, categories and GUID.
SPR-016 Parameters in families: Families that need FMC data in tags or schedules carry the shared parameter inside the family.
SPR-017 Manufacturer parameters kept: Manufacturer families keep their own parameters; FMC values are written beside them.
SPR-018 Built-ins first: Use a Revit built-in parameter wherever Revit has one.
SPR-019 Metric first: Parameters use metric units first (L/s, kW, Rw); BTU/h only as a label beside kW.
SPR-020 Codes on types: Element codes are type values, never instance values.
SPR-021 Geometry stage is instance: FMC_Geometry_Stage is an instance parameter holding G1–G5.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Sheets
reg_knowledge.body:
40 rules. Sources: STD, MAN
SHT-001 Sheet number pattern: Every sheet number is [Role]-[4 digits] using one of the twelve sheet roles.
SHT-002 Series meaning: The first digit gives the series: 0 general, 1 plans, 2 elevations, 3 sections, 4 details, 5 schedules, 6 3D, 7 setting-out, 8 logistics, 9 coordination.
SHT-003 Logistics on W-8xxx: Construction team logistics drawings use W-8xxx.
SHT-004 Z general sheets open every set: Every set opens with Z-0001 to Z-0006.
SHT-005 Sheets from the register: Create sheets only from FMC_Sheet_Register.csv; the tool never deletes or renames a sheet.
SHT-006 Placed items per register: Each sheet carries the views, legends and schedules the register's Placed column lists.
SHT-007 Issue set values: FMC_Issue_Set holds PERMIT, TENDER, CONSTRUCTION or RECORD, or several joined with +.
SHT-008 Sets by filter, not deletion: Make each issue set by filtering the sheet index on FMC_Issue_Set, never by deleting sheets.
SHT-009 RIBA stage to issue set: Map RIBA stages to issue sets: 4 → PERMIT and TENDER, 5 → CONSTRUCTION, 6–7 → RECORD; stages 0–3 issue Z-sheets and plans as information only.
SHT-010 RIBA stage sheet set content: Stage 2: Z-0001 plus A plans; stage 3: plus A elevations and sections and S/MEP plans; stage 4: all Core sheets; stage 5: Core plus the Optional sheets the BEP selects.
SHT-011 One title block: Every sheet uses FMC_TitleBlock, type A0, A1 or A3.
SHT-012 Sheet size: A1 landscape (841 × 594 mm) is the default; A3 is the half-size site set.
SHT-013 Border: The A1 border has a 20 mm binding margin on the left and 10 mm on the other sides, a 0.50 mm frame and an 8 × 6 grid.
SHT-014 Drawing area: Only viewports go in the 681 × 574 mm drawing area.
SHT-015 Information strip: The 130 mm strip on the right holds, top to bottom: brand, project, key plan, consultants, revisions, issue purpose, status, title, sign-off, number.
SHT-016 Labels only: Every word on the title block is a label; only field captions are typed.
SHT-017 Title block text sizes: Sheet number 12 mm, status 8 mm, current revision 6 mm, sheet name 5 mm, project name 3.5 mm bold, container name 1.8 mm.
SHT-018 Revisions from Revit: Revisions come from Revit's revision schedule and are never typed.
SHT-019 Sheet status: FMC_Sheet_Status holds the sheet's status code and FMC_Sheet_Status_Description explains it.
SHT-020 Status tint: The status box is tinted Formcraft Orange only when the status is S0 or S1.
SHT-021 Container name drives PDF: FMC_Container_Name holds the full ISO 19650 name and names the PDF.
SHT-022 Sheet parameters: Each sheet fills FMC_Sheet_Role, FMC_Sheet_Status, FMC_Issue_Set, FMC_Issue_Purpose, FMC_Volume, FMC_Level_Code and FMC_Container_Name.
SHT-023 Stamp is human: Only the registered professional, or their written instruction, switches FMC_Show_Professional_Stamp on.
SHT-024 Lockup by sub-brand: Use the main lockup for permit and pre-construction sets, Studio for design-only, Construction for role W; only one lockup on.
SHT-025 Logo placement: The logo is left-aligned in the strip, never centred or stretched.
SHT-026 View template on every sheet view: Every view on a sheet has a view template; WIP_ working views may not.
SHT-027 Plans carry key plan, north, scale bar: Every X-1xxx plan sheet has a key plan, north point and scale bar.
SHT-028 Role general and legend sheets: Each role has X-0001 general notes and design basis and X-0002 legend.
SHT-029 One plan sheet per level per system: Plans are one sheet per level per system.
SHT-030 Schedules from Revit: Schedule sheets show Revit schedules only, never typed tables.
SHT-031 Sheet index: Z-0001 carries Z10_Sheet_Index grouped by role, with number, name, current revision, revision date and status.
SHT-032 Drawing register with each issue: Export the drawing register (number, name, container name, status, revision) with every issue.
SHT-033 Scales: Use only 1:500, 1:200, 1:100, 1:50, 1:20, 1:10, 1:5 or 1:1.
SHT-034 PDF export: Export PDFs not combined, named by FMC_Container_Name, colour for coordination, black lines for construction, 300 dpi.
SHT-035 Sheet QA before issue: FMC_SheetQA reports zero sheets with issues before any issue.
SHT-036 Issue is a gate: Issuing a set is a human gate: revision and status set on every sheet, then the PIM authorises.
SHT-037 Sheet layout grid: Place viewports aligned to the 8 × 6 grid, titles bottom-left of each viewport, at least 10 mm apart, never over the strip.
SHT-038 Notes column placement: On X-0001 sheets, notes legends fill columns from the left of the drawing area.
SHT-039 Sheet completeness score: A sheet is complete when every Placed item exists, every view has a template, and no view is empty.
SHT-040 Stage parameter: Record the RIBA stage of each issue in the revision description until a dictionary parameter exists.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook: Sync
reg_knowledge.body:
24 rules. Sources: STD, MAN, RDM
SYN-001 Code format: Element codes are X.YYY_ZZ: one master-set letter, three-character group, two-digit variant.
SYN-002 Variant is an index: ZZ is a variant index, never a size.
SYN-003 Never delete or reuse: A code is never deleted or reused; retire it as Superseded with Superseded_By.
SYN-004 One code one spec: If rate, standard, material or performance differs, it is a new variant.
SYN-005 Codes on types only: Codes go on types, never on instances.
SYN-006 New codes by request: New codes come from the Data Owner by change form; nobody types a code not in the list.
SYN-007 Master workbook is source: FMC_Master_Data.xlsx is the source of record, each sheet with a named Data Owner.
SYN-008 Only approved data published: Only Approved rates and carbon factors and Verified standards leave the workbook.
SYN-009 Unverified standards blank: A standard reference not Verified stays blank in deliverables.
SYN-010 Publisher refuses on error: The publisher writes nothing if any error is found.
SYN-011 Keynote settings: Keynoting points at FMC_Keynotes.txt, Absolute (or At Library Location), numbering By keynotes, showing 21 master sets.
SYN-012 Sync dry run first: Run the master data sync as a dry run first, then for real in one transaction.
SYN-013 Sync cadence: Sync daily and before every issue.
SYN-014 Sync behaviour: Copy the keynote to FMC_Keynote_Code, overwrite master-controlled fields and clear stale text.
SYN-015 Unpriced marker: Types with no approved rate get 'UNPRICED - no approved rate' in FMC_Rate_Source_Date.
SYN-016 Change log: Every value changed is logged in a CSV: type, parameter, before, after.
SYN-017 Invalid codes fixed by picking: Invalid codes are fixed by picking again from the list.
SYN-018 Missing code is a change request: A keynote code missing from the kit is a kit change request.
SYN-019 Preview Read, apply Setup: Sync preview is Read class; sync apply is Setup class.
SYN-020 Scripts write data only: Sync writes only master-owned fields; never geometry or structural sections.
SYN-021 Schedules by code: Schedules group by FMC_Keynote_Code and show FMC_Code_Description, never retyped text.
SYN-022 Waste factor for counted items: Counted manufactured items carry waste factor 1.00.
SYN-023 Never type rates: Rates are never typed into a model or BoQ; they come from approved master data.
SYN-024 Kit outputs never hand-edited: Change the kit source and rebuild; never edit an output by hand.

TPL-001 Template set: There is one Base template and twelve role templates: A, I, S, M, E, P, FP, LP, C, L, Z and W.
TPL-002 Base is master only: Never start a project from the Base template.
TPL-003 Change Base first: Change common items in Base, push them with Transfer Project Standards (changed items only), then bump the version.
TPL-004 Project units: Set length mm (0 dp), area m² (2 dp), volume m³ (3 dp), angle ° (2 dp), slope %, currency UGX (0 dp).

TPL-006 Keynote file: Point keynoting at FMC_Keynotes.txt by absolute path, numbering By keynotes.
TPL-007 Project Information placeholders: All Group 01 Project Information fields exist and hold TBC so blanks show.
TPL-008 Coded system types: Wall, floor, roof and ceiling types come from the starter library, each with its code, plus finish-only types for G4.
TPL-009 Materials: Materials are FMC_ named with appearance assets mapped for visualisation.
TPL-010 Revision numbering: Revision numbering uses prefix P with two digits (P01…) and a second sequence with prefix C.
TPL-011 Browser organisation: Views are organised by Role > View type > Purpose; sheets by Series 0xxx–9xxx.
TPL-012 View templates from kit: Build the 81 kit view templates in Base and push them to the role templates.
TPL-013 Filters from kit: Build the 42 rule-based filters with the fixed kit colours.
TPL-014 Modelling views: Every template has Z_3D_Model_Review, Z_3D_Warnings and A_FP_Lxx_Model working plans.
TPL-015 QA views: Every template has the three QA views: no code red, unpriced orange, no stage yellow.
TPL-016 Review and export views: Every template carries VT_Z_3D_ModelReview and VT_Z_3D_Export, and the views Z_3D_NWC_Export and Z_3D_IFC_Export.
TPL-017 QA schedules: Every template has the 00–09 QA and pre-construction schedules in folder 00_QA_and_Precon.
TPL-018 Export setups: Templates hold IFC setups FMC_IFC4_RV and FMC_IFC4X3, the NWC options and the PDF naming rule.
TPL-019 Worksets: Create Z_Grids_Levels, Z_Links_<Role>, <Role>_Shell, <Role>_Interior, <Role>_Site and, for MEP, <Role>_<System>.
TPL-020 Text types: Text types run FMC_Arial_1.8 to FMC_Arial_7.0_Bold, all Arial.
TPL-021 Line weights and patterns: Use eight line weights 0.10–1.00 mm, six line patterns and twelve fill patterns from the kit.
TPL-022 No graphics created in projects: Nobody creates a text type or fill pattern in a project; missing items go to the BIM Manager for Base.
TPL-023 Voltage definitions: Base has the voltages 240 V, 415 V, 11 kV and 33 kV at ±10%.
TPL-024 Distribution systems: Base has the four distribution systems DS_33kV_3Ph_3W, DS_11kV_3Ph_3W, DS_415-240V_3Ph_4W and DS_240V_1Ph_2W.

TPL-026 Phases: Use only the phases Existing, Demolition and New Construction.

reg_knowledge.title: BIM rulebook index, gaps and conflicts
reg_knowledge.body:
# Formcraft Revit MCP: rulebook index (0.1-draft, kit 2.2)

Sources: **STD** = FMC-BIM-STD-002 v2.2 (Revit families, sheets and annotation standard); **MAN** = FMC-BIM-MAN-001 v2.2 (Master Manual & BEP Framework). Plugin rules come from **RDM** (`FMC_MCP/ROADMAP.md`, decisions D1–D5) and **CLM** (`FMC_MCP/CLAUDE.md`, hard rules 1–6). All of these are tagged `from_standard` with their real clause. `proposed` rules have `clause: null` and need BIM Manager approval.

| Feature | File | Rules | from_standard (STD/MAN) | from_standard (RDM/CLM) | proposed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Naming | FMC_Rulebook_Naming.json | 39 | 36 | 1 | 2 |
| Templates | FMC_Rulebook_Templates.json | 33 | 29 | 4 | 0 |
| SharedParameters | FMC_Rulebook_SharedParameters.json | 21 | 20 | 1 | 0 |
| Families | FMC_Rulebook_Families.json | 43 | 34 | 8 | 1 |
| ProjectStart | FMC_Rulebook_ProjectStart.json | 24 | 15 | 8 | 1 |
| Sheets | FMC_Rulebook_Sheets.json | 40 | 34 | 0 | 6 |
| Annotation | FMC_Rulebook_Annotation.json | 35 | 25 | 0 | 10 |
| QA | FMC_Rulebook_QA.json | 31 | 27 | 3 | 1 |
| LinksAndCoordinates | FMC_Rulebook_LinksAndCoordinates.json | 27 | 23 | 3 | 1 |
| Sync | FMC_Rulebook_Sync.json | 24 | 22 | 2 | 0 |
| ClaudeUse | FMC_Rulebook_ClaudeUse.json | 27 | 6 | 18 | 3 |
| **Total** | | **344** | **271** | **48** | **25** |

## Gaps and conflicts

### Gaps (the plugin needs it; neither document says it)

1. **RIBA stages are not used anywhere.** Neither STD nor MAN mentions RIBA. They use ISO 19650 delivery stages and gates G1–G3 (MAN 3.2), geometry stages G1–G5 (MAN 3.3, 9.5) and `FMC_Issue_Set` = PERMIT/TENDER/CONSTRUCTION/RECORD (STD 2.4). The RIBA-to-issue-set map and the stage sheet sets (SHT-009, SHT-010) are proposed. There is also no dictionary parameter for the stage (SHT-040, proposed). This needs a decision: either adopt RIBA, with a dictionary change request, or key the Sheets Manager on the issue set and G-stage.
2. **Annotation density and tidy rules.** The documents fix fonts, heights, tag behaviour and legends. They say nothing about how much to annotate at each stage, overlap clearance, leader use, how dimensions reference elements, or value overrides (ANN-026 to ANN-035, proposed). The only stage signal is permit vs construction view templates (STD 7; VT_A_FloorPlan_Permit has "no construction notes").
3. **Sheet layout.** STD 3.1 fixes the title block geometry and the 681 × 574 mm drawing area, which holds viewports only. Nothing covers where viewports go, the spacing between them or where view titles sit (SHT-037, SHT-038). There is also no definition of a "complete" sheet beyond the FMC_SheetQA checks (SHT-039).
4. **View and level naming is open.** RDM decision D3 is open. MAN 4.6 gives a view pattern (`A_FP_L01_General`) but has no level-name rule (NAM-023 is proposed). QA treats these as warnings only.
5. **Dimension styles.** The Graphics tab says only "FMC_Arial_2.5 … Notes, tags, dimensions". No dimension type names, tick marks, witness-line gaps or rounding are stated.
6. **Project families in the Manual.** D4 (`[Project]_[Role]_…rfa` in `01_WIP\<Role>\Families\`) exists only in RDM. ROADMAP itself says "Manual 4.6 needs the matching line (a Manual change request)".
7. **Default project roles and recipe default sizes** are not stated (PST-024, FAM-043, proposed).

### Conflicts and inconsistencies

1. **Sheet status list.** MAN 4.4 lists S0–S4, S6, S7, A1/A2…, B1/B2…, CR, with no S5. STD 3.1 says `FMC_Sheet_Status (S0–S7, A1, B1, CR)`, which implies S5 and only A1/B1. SHT-019 carries both lists. The plugin should follow MAN 4.4 (MAN precedence, order item 4 over 5) until STD is corrected.
2. **Who sets demand factors.** STD 5.3 says demand factors "are set per load classification in the same dialog", with starting values in Electrical_Settings, approved by the engineer. MAN 17.1 lists FMC_SetupElectricalSettings as setting "demand factors (STD-002 5.3)". CLM rule 5 and RDM Phase 2 say tools never set them. TPL-025 follows the plugin rule, so MAN 17.1 and STD 5.3 need a note that the MCP port leaves them blank.
3. **Fill pattern count.** STD 6.3 says "twelve fill patterns", but the kit Graphics tab lists 13 (FMC_Blockwork … FMC_Solid). This is a kit or STD fix.
4. **Dictionary deprecated list.** MAN Part 5 names the deprecated items as "Project Name, Client Name, Drawn By, Checked By, Approved By, Current Revision … (the plot fields)". STD 3.2 names `FMC_Project_Name, FMC_Appointing_Party, FMC_Sheet_Revision, FMC_Drawn_By, FMC_Checked_By, FMC_Approved_By, FMC_Plot_District`. The lists agree in count but not in naming. SPR-002 uses the STD list, which matches the kit file names.
5. **QA view names.** MAN 9.10 names the views `Z_3D_QA_NoCode / _Unpriced / _NoStage` and `Z_3D_Model_Review`. STD 7 and the kit use view templates `VT_Z_3D_QA`, `VT_Z_3D_ModelReview` and `VT_Z_3D_Export` (one export template vs MAN's two export views). STD 4.2 refers to "The VT_Z_3D_QA view". Treat VT_ names as templates and Z_ names as views (TPL-015, TPL-016).
6. **Text heights below 2.5 mm.** STD 3.1 gives a 1.8 mm minimum for A3 text, but MAN 9.14 lists only 2.5/3.5/5 mm. The 1.8 mm container-name strip falls outside the MAN heights. This is minor, but a text-height checker must allow 1.8 mm on title blocks.
7. **Model-class lock wording.** CLM rule 1 includes `tag_*` and `color_splash` among model-changing tools, while RDM 4 lists Model class as `WRITE_COMMANDS` only. If annotation tools (Annotation Master) count as `tag_*`, they are locked on live models even with the D1 toggle on. That blocks Annotation Master on live projects until a new decision.

Note: the MAN Order of precedence puts the manual above templates, scripts and the kit. Where STD (a companion standard) and MAN disagree, neither document states which wins. A precedence line for STD vs MAN is itself a gap.

Give the building control authority the notice it requires before each stage inspection (V: Building Control Regulations, 2020): 1 setting out and foundation excavation; 2 foundations and DPC; 3 superstructure and ring beam; 4 roof structure before covering; 5 drainage before backfilling; 6 completion before occupation. 4. Verify existing conditions, levels and services on site before setting out or ordering materials.
5. Order of precedence unless the contract says otherwise: contract conditions, specification, drawings at the larger scale, drawings at the smaller scale, schedules.

7. Setting out is from the survey control points on Z-0005. The survey point is never moved.

2. Each submittal carries the designer's name and registration, the design basis and calculations, and drawings that reference these sheet numbers.
3. The designer of record reviews each submittal for compliance with the design intent and returns it marked within the period in the contract.

=== LG_Z_Closeout: CONTRACT CLOSEOUT AND PRACTICAL COMPLETION ===
1. As-built record: model and drawings updated to what was built (G5), issued with status CR.
2. Operation and maintenance manuals, warranties and test certificates for every system, linked from the asset data (FMC_OM_Link).
3. Commissioning records signed by the installer and witnessed by the designer.
4. Final clean, keys and access cards handed over with a signed schedule.
5. Stamp boxes: registered architect, registered engineer, physical planning authority.

=== LG_Z_CodeSummary: CODE SUMMARY AND GOVERNING STANDARDS ===
Acts and regulations (V): Building Control Act, 2013; Building Control Regulations, 2020; Physical Planning Act, 2010; National Environment Act, 2019; Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2006; Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019.
Building code (V): National Building Code, 2019 and the National Building (Structural Design) Code, 2019.
Design standards are listed by discipline on X-0001. Every reference is checked against the Standards Register before release; withdrawn standards are not cited.
Building classification: [FMC_Building_Class]. Fire resistance periods per the fire strategy on FP-0001.

=== LG_Z_BIMStatement: BIM INFORMATION STATEMENT ===
These drawings are produced from the federated information model listed in the model register. The model is the source; the drawing is a view.
Each model is named to ISO 19650 (container name), carries a suitability status, and is modelled to the geometry stage stated (G1-G5).
Information is delivered to the Level of Information Need set in the BEP (ISO 7817-1).

reg_knowledge.title: Material library: 225 materials and 39 raw materials
reg_knowledge.body:
Each material has class, keynote code, cost code, graphics, texture maps, discipline, description, makers, origin, standard and price. 85 have prices (now in the Price book). 140 new keynotes proposed.
Research gaps recorded in the kit:
- UNBS catalogue (31 Dec 2023 PDF) blocked automated access: open it by hand for bricks, blocks, ISSB, BRC mesh, aggregates, glass, plywood/MDF/gypsum, ceramic tiles, paving blocks, kerbs, PPR, uPVC profiles, membranes, insulation, extinguishers.
- Supplier quotes needed for all secondary prices (Aura Build, Smeaton, Lexa, Jiji.ug, Edremedystock) before BoQ use; the 12 mm rebar price differs 20-30% between sources.
- No prices: ready-mix concrete by grade, ISSB, kerbs, precast pipes/manholes, structural sections, Y25/Y32 bars, stone-coated tiles, Safal/MRM sheets, fibre-cement and polycarbonate sheets.
- No prices: glass per m2, aluminium/steel/uPVC windows, doors, burglar bars, insect mesh, ironmongery.
- No prices: Mvule, Mahogany and other hardwoods; cypress; MDF; melamine; HPL; quartz/granite worktops (2010 data only).
- No prices: Sadolin/Crown/Basco paints, 4 L gloss, porcelain 60x60 specifically, waterproofing, insulation.
- No prices: HDPE, pressure PVC 1/2-1 inch, Crestanks tanks, Cable Corporation cable, MCB/DB, earth rods, copper tape, GI/copper pipe, ductwork, Armaflex, sprinkler pipe, hose reels, PV modules.
- No prices: topsoil, Paspalum/Kikuyu turf per m2, mulch, pebbles, decking, asphalt, gabions, geotextile.
- Old prices kept with their dates (escalate or replace): ceilings Apr 2017, gypsum 12 mm Nov 2020, grass seed 2017.
- Jiji.ug listings carry no date and often no unit (tiles 40x40, armoured cable, trunking, Weatherguard 'bucket').
- Concrete block face size 450 x 225 has no Ugandan primary source; Uganda Clays interlocking/partition face sizes assumed from units per m2; adobe unit size assumed.
- ISSB: UN-Habitat gives 265 x 140 x 100 (face 265 x 100 in a 140 wall) but the kit pattern/texture use 265 x 140; cement content (5-10%?) and thermal data unverified (open the UN-Habitat PDF).
- Kit keynote X.TAP_00 says 25 x 3 mm copper tape; the 2019 Electrical Installations Code para 35 says 20 x 3 mm (X.TAP_03 proposed). Confirm which the kit keeps.
- Kit keynotes B.225_00/01 describe 225 x 112 x 75 facing brick; Uganda Clays sells 220 x 38 x 75 half bricks (B.225_02 proposed). B.ISB_00 says 150 mm; UN-Habitat ISSB gives a 140 mm wall.
- Cement market shares are from 2018; Kampala Cement in receivership (29 Jun 2026); Mombasa Cement Tororo and Dangote presence unconfirmed.
- Rebar makers beyond Tembo and Tororo Cement (Roofings Rolling Mills, Steel & Tube, Pramukh, Sujal, MMI) unverified.
- Twyford brand link to Goodwill Uganda Ceramic unverified; Kapeeka tile sizes not published.
- Current Sadolin/Crown and Basco Uganda product lines and colour charts not verified; all paint hex values are placeholders.
- Roofings/Uganda Baati colour hex values are approximations, not RAL data; Romantile, Orientile, CoverMax, Resincot and Lifestile colours/profiles need the maker's chart.
- Timber: Mvule legal status (protected list), NaFORRI properties for Musizi, Nkoba, Mugavu, Podo, Elgon olive; Nkoba species identity; standard sawn sizes and CCA retention not sourced.
- No Ugandan source: uPVC windows, float/tempered glass processors, gypsum brands beyond Jiji listings, PVC ceilings, cabro/kerb/terrazzo makers, Sika/Fosroc, insulation, wall putty, gabions, geotextiles.
- MEP makers unverified: switchgear brands, cable tray makers, GI pipe, Armaflex distributor, PV module and solar water heater suppliers (UECCC 2024 lists not opened), extinguisher standard.
- PPR colour (green or white), HDPE stripe convention and fire-pipe red paint spec not verified for Uganda.
- MoWT Series 3000/4000 text (CBR, gradings, binder grades) and KCCA/UNRA unit rates not obtained.
- Lime suppliers and prices, Lwera sand-mining restrictions (NEMA), quarry names (Muyenga, Mukono, Namanve) unverified.
- Vernacular: thatch species, papyrus/banana-fibre suppliers, bamboo species, adobe/wattle-and-daub thermal data not sourced.
- Physical values (density, conductivity) are generic engineering values, not Ugandan tests; carbon notes are generic estimates except the Makerere kiln figure.

reg_knowledge.title: Formcraft BIM kit v2.2 r4: what is in it
reg_knowledge.body: Standard: FMC-BIM-MAN-001 v2.2 (Master Manual and BEP) and FMC-BIM-STD-002 v2.2 (families, sheets, annotation). Folders: 01 shared parameters (178 in 30 groups), 02 keynotes, 03 master data (codes, family register and specs, sheet register, legends, rulebooks, design values, recipes), 04 families (staged recipes; built families in releases), 05 scripts, 06 patterns and templates (Base + 12 role templates), 07 IFC/IDS and materials (with textures), 08 Navisworks, 09 manual and training, 10 drawing notes, 11 brand lockups. Build and test: _build/build_all.py and test_kit.py. Update packages r1-r6 in _updates.
